title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that evaluated whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—shared initial LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) + deterministic Batfish‑style validator + at most one automated LLM repair—reduces verifier‑detected semantic/safety failures on intent→vendor‑CLI tasks. Planned N=300 pairs; after preregistered exclusions 266 complete pairs were analysed. Baseline passes = 260/266 (97.744%); final guarded (GVR) passes = 265/266 (99.624%). Paired difference = 0.01879699248; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. Paired bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Repair was invoked in 6 repair calls. Under the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule the observed improvement does not reach confirmatory significance; inference is limited by very small discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0). The preregistered secondary confirmatory hypothesis H2 comprised two parts: (a) median repair iterations per task < 5 (confirmed; median = 0 based on archived provider_call_audit where repair calls = 6 across 300 tasks), and (b) median end‑to‑end per‑task latency ≤ 60 s (not computable from archived per‑episode timestamps; latency therefore was not assessed and remains an untested confirmatory item). We present preregistered design details, deterministic validation rules, recorded runtime model settings, complete numeric results, contamination findings (no flagged duplicates), and an evidence‑grounded discussion of validity threats. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: LLMs are increasingly explored for NetOps tasks such as intent→vendor‑CLI translation and zero‑touch configuration generation. Stochastic generation can produce syntactic or semantic violations that threaten network safety; generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures that interpose deterministic validators (e.g., Batfish‑style tools) and bounded repair loops have been proposed to improve correctness. We executed a preregistered paired experiment to measure the validator‑triggered repair benefit under shared_initial_candidate semantics: the same single initial sampled candidate is used by both baseline and guarded arms, and only the guarded arm may trigger deterministic validation and at most one automated repair. Research question: Does a GVR pipeline (LLM initial candidate + deterministic verifier + ≤1 automated repair) reduce verifier‑detected failures relative to the same initial candidate with no repair? Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑archived confirmatory evaluation that reports exact paired inference, bootstrap intervals, a preregistered sensitivity analysis for missingness, and a concise discussion of operational limitations.
sections.related_work: Prior work documents intent‑to‑CLI prototypes, benchmarks, and proposals to integrate deterministic verifiers or GVR loops to reduce hallucinations and semantic errors [1–5]. Surveys emphasize grounding strategies (RAG, tool augmentation) and the importance of deterministic validation to bound risk. Network verification tools (Batfish, header‑space analyses) have been proposed as oracles inside LLM‑driven pipelines. Our study differs by executing a preregistered paired test with shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic validator traces, and archived raw artifacts to support reproducible confirmatory inference.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The preregistration identifier is cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics and N=300 intent pairs (150 Cisco‑like, 150 Juniper‑like) sampled deterministically from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator. Execution contract mandated one initial model generation per task and at most one automated repair call if the deterministic validator failed. Deterministic validation: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performs syntactic parsing, required‑sequence checks, and reachability/constraint checks and yields a binary pass/fail outcome that served as the primary endpoint. Recorded model configuration: execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd) declares declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini, max_output_tokens = 1024, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, provider = openai_responses, and temperature = null (unset); archived configuration contains no deterministic sampling seed (nondeterminism cannot be excluded and is disclosed). Execution accounting: planned episodes = 600, completed episodes = 532, failed episodes = 68, complete paired units analysed = 266; retry and exclusion rules followed the preregistration. Analysis: primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes; paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) for the primary 266‑pair analysis; sensitivity analysis 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treats excluded both‑arm failures (34 pairs) as double failures to produce a conservative paired table on the full planned N=300. Contamination detection: archived contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged duplicates (no exact public duplicates were detected), thus no items were excluded for contamination from the primary analysis.
sections.results: Primary confirmatory results (complete paired analysis, n=266): baseline successes = 260/266 (0.9774436090); guarded final successes = 265/266 (0.9962406015). Paired contingency (guarded,baseline): n11=260, n10=5, n01=0, n00=1 (see Table 1). Paired difference = 0.01879699248. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625 (preregistered α=0.05 → not significant). Paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Provider_call_audit(stage_counts) records shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 6 (six repair calls executed). From that audit, the distribution of repair iterations per task yields median repair iterations = 0 (confirming preregistered H2(a): median < 5). Per‑task end‑to‑end latency was not recorded in the archived per‑episode artifacts and therefore H2(b) (median latency ≤ 60 s) could not be evaluated and remains untested. Missingness: 34 episodes were excluded as both‑arm provider/infra failures per the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule; sensitivity analysis treating these as failures (N=300) gives baseline = 260/300 (0.866667), guarded = 265/300 (0.883333), paired difference = 0.016667, exact McNemar p = 0.0625 (discordant counts unchanged); approximate 95% CI (paired normal approximation using archived discordant counts for N=300) = [0.00220, 0.03114]. Repair‑invocation histogram: 6 tasks triggered the automated repair stage (Figure 2). Contamination: archived contamination_summary.csv reports no flagged duplicates.
sections.discussion: The guarded GVR pipeline produced a small absolute improvement (≈1.88 percentage points on complete pairs; ≈1.67 pp on planned N). Under the preregistered exact‑McNemar decision rule the improvement did not reach α=0.05 (p=0.0625). The inferential discrepancy between a bootstrap CI that excludes zero and an exact McNemar p > 0.05 arises from method mechanics: the two‑sided exact McNemar depends only on discordant counts (here n10=5, n01=0) and is discrete—thus a two‑sided exact p can exceed 0.05 even when a resampling CI excludes zero. Practically, the low repair invocation rate (6/300) indicates most initial candidates already satisfied the deterministic validator for this model and task corpus, leaving limited headroom for guarded repair to improve outcomes. Limitations that constrain generalisability include (i) shared_initial_candidate semantics—our estimand measures validator‑triggered repair benefit for a fixed initial sample and does not compare alternative first‑pass constrained generation strategies; (ii) validator coverage—deterministic_netops_validator_v5 checks a finite set of syntactic/semantic properties and cannot detect violations outside its rule set; (iii) sample and missingness—34 both‑arm infrastructure/model failures reduced the analysed pair count to 266; (iv) runtime nondeterminism—temperature was unset in the archived model configuration and no deterministic sampling seed is present; archived calls therefore may reflect nondeterministic generation; (v) latency H2(b) was not archived and could not be assessed. Operationally, these results show that deterministic validators can provide reliable pass/fail assurance and enable bounded automated repair, but observed marginal benefit depends strongly on baseline pass rates and on repair‑convertibility of the remaining errors. Future work should target corpora with higher baseline failure rates, alternative generation/constrained‑decoding strategies, expanded validator coverage, and systematic latency measurement and human‑in‑the‑loop escalation studies.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered paired experiment with shared_initial_candidate semantics evaluated a GVR pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + ≤1 automated repair) on intent→CLI tasks. Across 266 analysed pairs the guarded pipeline improved verifier pass rate by 0.01880 but did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule (p=0.0625). Paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) narrowly excludes zero. Median repair iterations per task = 0 (H2(a) satisfied). Median end‑to‑end latency (H2(b)) was not recorded in per‑episode archived artifacts and therefore that confirmatory item could not be evaluated. Repair calls were rare (6), limiting the guarded pipeline's observable benefit for this corpus. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived to enable independent reanalysis and follow‑on studies.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory disclosure (concise): Models and orchestration—declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, sha256: 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd); orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration—cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Initial master prompt—immutable archived reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary—before the autonomy lock a human Research Director selected the topic family and approved pre‑lock infrastructure development; after the autonomy lock the study design selection, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, peer review simulation, and revision were performed autonomously by the registered pipeline; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Reproducibility pointers—execution and analysis artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv, contamination_summary.csv, analysis logs) are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle (representative artifact hashes are recorded in the archived manifest). Nondeterminism disclosure—the archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset) and contains no deterministic sampling seed; therefore nondeterministic sampling of model outputs cannot be excluded from the recorded calls.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both arms began from the same single sampled candidate per preregistration; the measured estimand is strictly the validator‑triggered repair benefit and does not evaluate alternative first‑pass constrained prompts or independent generation strategies.

Missingness and sample reduction: planned N=300 pairs; after infrastructure/provider exclusions 266 pairs were complete and 34 both‑arm episodes were excluded per preregistered rules, reducing effective sample size and precision.
Small discordant counts: primary inference used exact McNemar with few discordants (n10=5, n01=0); conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 checks a finite battery of syntactic/semantic/reachability rules; semantic violations outside its coverage are possible and unmeasured.
Runtime nondeterminism and sampling: archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null and no deterministic seed; nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for recorded model calls.

H2 latency not evaluated: the preregistered H2 combined median repair iterations and median end‑to‑end latency ≤ 60 s—median repair iterations = 0 (archived provider_call_audit supports this), but per‑episode end‑to‑end latency was not present in archived per‑task artifacts and therefore H2(b) could not be assessed.

External validity: tasks derive from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal benefit across other vendors, larger network topologies, or production deployments.
